title: Air India Courts UK Travel Trade in London During World Travel Market
excerpt: The airline hosted diaspora-heavy UK travel sellers with Tourism Minister Shekhawat, building on its new tourism-promotion MoU with the ministry.
body:
• Air India hosted senior UK travel trade leaders in London on the sidelines of World Travel Market (WTM) London, alongside Union Tourism and Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat.
  • Attendees included Southall Travel, Brightsun Travel, TUI, Trailfinders, Kuoni, Expedia, Trip.com and Akbar Travels, plus representatives from London Gatwick Airport.
  • The discussions centred on growing inbound tourism to India and follow a recently signed MoU between Air India and the Ministry of Tourism to jointly promote India internationally.
  • For diaspora travellers, the push pairs the UK's large India-focused travel trade — much of it diaspora-run — with India's effort to position itself as an aviation and transit hub.

Air India has hosted UK travel industry leaders in London for an evening of discussions on growing inbound tourism to India, alongside Union Minister of Tourism and Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat. The gathering was held on the sidelines of World Travel Market London, the annual travel trade exhibition running November 3 to 5 at ExCeL London.

Who was in the room

Senior representatives attended from Southall Travel, Brightsun Travel, Moresand, Skylord Travels, Carlton Leisure, TUI, Trailfinders, Kuoni, Expedia, Trip.com and Akbar Travels — a list that mixes global platforms with the UK's established South Asian travel agencies. London Gatwick Airport also sent representatives, bringing an airport perspective on how airlines, travel sellers and tourism authorities can support international visitor growth. Goa Tourism Minister Rohan Ashok Khaunte and Rajya Sabha member Sudha Murty were also present at the gathering.

What was discussed

The event provided a platform for discussions on strengthening inbound tourism to India, unlocking growth opportunities across key international source markets, and showcasing India's cultural, heritage and nature-based tourism offerings to global travellers. The United Kingdom is one of India's most significant inbound source markets, with strong diaspora ties and deep interest in heritage travel.

The MoU behind it

The London evening follows a recently signed memorandum of understanding between Air India and India's Ministry of Tourism to jointly promote the country as a premier global tourism destination and support its development as an aviation and transit hub. No new routes or commercial agreements were announced at the event; its purpose was trade relationship-building at the point in the year when UK sellers plan the coming seasons' India programmes.

Part of a wider WTM push

The Air India evening sat inside a broader Indian presence at this year's World Travel Market. Shekhawat also inaugurated the Incredible India Pavilion at the exhibition alongside UK Minister for Tourism Stephanie Peacock MP, a joint appearance the ministry framed as a signal of deepening bilateral tourism cooperation between India and the United Kingdom. For UK-based diaspora travellers, the trade being courted in London this week is the same trade that sells most of their India trips: family-run agencies in Southall and Leicester alongside global platforms such as Expedia and Trip.com, all of which were represented at the Air India event.
